analysis.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject of וַיִּבְרָא. The repeated object marker אֶת introduces what God created: the great sea creatures, the living creatures that swarm in the waters, and the winged birds.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ.

analysis.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject of וַיִּבְרָא (“and he created”). The third-person masculine singular verb identifies God as the one who created the great sea creatures.
analysis.morphology: Masculine plural absolute common noun with singular reference.

analysis.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject of וַיִּבְרָא ‘created’. אֶת introduces הַתַּנִּינִם הַגְּדֹלִים ‘the great sea creatures’ as the first definite direct object. The following objects are each introduced by וְאֵת.
analysis.morphology: Direct-object particle in the short form אֶת, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: The adjective הַגְּדֹלִים agrees with הַתַּנִּינִם in gender, number, and definiteness, giving “the great sea monsters.” The following reference to creatures swarming in the waters supports the aquatic sense.
analysis.morphology: Masculine plural absolute noun with prefixed definite article הַ־.

analysis.evidence: In הַתַּנִּינִם הַגְּדֹלִים, the adjective agrees with הַתַּנִּינִם in gender, number, and definiteness and describes the physical size of the sea creatures.
analysis.morphology: Attributive adjective, masculine plural absolute, with the definite article הַ־.

analysis.evidence: כָּל governs the singular נֶפֶשׁ in כָּל נֶפֶשׁ הַחַיָּה הָרֹמֶשֶׂת, “every living creature that moves.” It includes each creature described by the following clause אֲשֶׁר שָׁרְצוּ הַמַּיִם, “with which the waters swarmed.”
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: כָּל נֶפֶשׁ הַחַיָּה הָרֹמֶשֶׂת means “every living creature that moves.” Both הַחַיָּה and הָרֹמֶשֶׂת are feminine singular and describe נֶפֶשׁ. The following clause identifies these creatures as those with which the waters swarmed.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, singular absolute, with feminine agreement

analysis.evidence: In כָּל נֶפֶשׁ הַחַיָּה הָרֹמֶשֶׂת, both הַחַיָּה (“living”) and הָרֹמֶשֶׂת (“moving”) describe the feminine singular נֶפֶשׁ (“creature”). The following clause identifies the waters as teeming with these creatures.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular absolute adjective with the definite article הַ.

analysis.evidence: הָרֹמֶשֶׂת agrees with the feminine singular נֶפֶשׁ in כָּל נֶפֶשׁ הַחַיָּה הָרֹמֶשֶׂת, “every living creature that moves about.” The following clause אֲשֶׁר שָׁרְצוּ הַמַּיִם identifies these as creatures with which the waters swarmed.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הָ־ + Qal active participle, feminine singular absolute, used attributively.

analysis.evidence: אֲשֶׁר links כָּל נֶפֶשׁ הַחַיָּה הָרֹמֶשֶׂת to שָׁרְצוּ הַמַּיִם, describing every moving living creature with which the waters swarmed. הַמַּיִם is the subject of שָׁרְצוּ.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected relative particle without prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Add a root article for שרצ with the Qal verb שָׁרַץ and its sense in Genesis 1:20.
draft.definition: Of waters, to teem with living creatures.
draft.evidence: In Genesis 1:20 the waters are commanded to teem. Genesis 1:21 repeats the verb when it describes the living creatures with which the waters teemed.

analysis.evidence: The plural verb שָׁרְצוּ agrees with its following subject הַמַּיִם, “the waters.” The relative clause אֲשֶׁר שָׁרְצוּ הַמַּיִם describes the living creatures “with which the waters teemed,” echoing the command in Genesis 1:20.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person common plural.
analysis.sense: Of waters, to teem with living creatures.

analysis.evidence: לְמִינֵהֶם groups the creatures that swarm in the waters by kind. The parallel לְמִינֵהוּ applies the same grouping to winged birds, with a singular suffix referring to the collective עוֹף.
analysis.morphology: Preposition לְ ‘according to’ + masculine singular construct noun מִין + third-person masculine plural possessive suffix ‘their’.

draft.change: Add Gen.1.21 as an example of the existing אֵת … וְאֵת construction in article et.
draft.definition: אֵת introduces a direct object and can be repeated before successive objects of the same verb.
draft.evidence: In Gen.1.21, וְאֵת כָּל עוֹף כָּנָף introduces the last group of creatures governed by וַיִּבְרָא.

analysis.evidence: וַיִּבְרָא אֱלֹהִים ‘God created’ governs a list of three objects. At position 14, וְ joins כָּל עוֹף כָּנָף ‘every winged bird’ to that list, and אֵת marks the whole phrase as the third object.
analysis.morphology: Prefixed coordinating conjunction וְ ‘and’ + direct-object particle אֵת, without a suffix.
analysis.sense: Marks the following noun phrase as a direct object of the verb.

analysis.evidence: כָּל quantifies עוֹף כָּנָף in the phrase “every winged bird.” The following לְמִינֵהוּ, “according to its kind,” supports the distributive reading.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular noun in the construct state, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In כָּל עוֹף כָּנָף, “every winged bird,” כָּנָף means “wing” and identifies the creatures in view. The singular suffix in לְמִינֵהוּ, “according to its kind,” agrees with the collective עוֹף.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular collective noun, with no prefix or suffix. Its form is identical in the absolute and construct states.

analysis.evidence: In כָּל עוֹף כָּנָף, literally “every bird of wing,” כָּנָף names the body part that characterizes the bird. The phrase means “every winged bird.”
analysis.morphology: Common noun, feminine singular absolute, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In כָּל עוֹף כָּנָף לְמִינֵהוּ, the singular suffix refers to עוֹף. The phrase describes each winged creature according to its kind, paralleling לְמִינֵהֶם earlier in the verse.
analysis.morphology: Preposition לְ + masculine singular construct noun + third-person masculine singular possessive suffix.

analysis.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject of וַיַּרְא. The clause כִּי טוֹב gives the content of what God saw: what he had created was good.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־
analysis.sense: see or perceive that something is so

analysis.evidence: In וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים כִּי טוֹב, “God saw that it was good,” אֱלֹהִים is the subject of the third-person masculine singular verb וַיַּרְא. It refers to the same creator named in the opening words וַיִּבְרָא אֱלֹהִים.
analysis.morphology: Masculine plural absolute common noun with singular verbal agreement.

draft.change: Clarify the existing Gen.3.6 citation under ki-that by identifying the role of the second כִּי.
draft.definition: After a verb of perception, כִּי introduces what is perceived.
draft.evidence: In Gen.3.6 the repeated כִּי introduces a second clause governed by וַתֵּרֶא, and the prefixed וְ coordinates it with the first.

analysis.evidence: In וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים כִּי טוֹב, כִּי introduces what God saw, “that it was good.”
analysis.morphology: Uninflected subordinating conjunction with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Introduces the content of what is seen.

analysis.evidence: After God creates the creatures of the waters and the winged birds, וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים כִּי טוֹב means “God saw that it was good.” טוֹב expresses God’s judgment of what he has just created.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute adjective used predicatively, without prefix or suffix.
